media.provenance: Llewellyn et al. 2023, Plants 12(3):422, Figure 5; repository original images/reference/original/mdpi-cannabis-calcium-deficiency-figure-5.png

observations.finding: The figure is a controlled flowering-stage temporal sequence rather than one independent field photograph.
observations.plant_location: lower to upper canopy over time
observations.pattern: necrotic spotting and marginal necrosis with later upper-tip curl

observations.finding: The visible pattern is compatible with calcium-withholding injury in this experiment but is not by itself a field confirmation rule.

differential.label: calcium deficiency / calcium-withholding injury
discriminating_checks: Confirm substrate/root-zone conditions and calcium availability.
Compare progression and tissue distribution; use plant/context data rather than appearance alone.

differential.label: root-zone or environmental stress with overlapping necrosis/curl
discriminating_checks: Check root-zone pH/EC, irrigation, temperature and recent environmental stress.

uncertainty.reason: The source confirms a controlled calcium-withholding treatment, but a field image with a similar appearance does not establish the same cause without context.

evidence.citation: Llewellyn D, Golem S, Jones AMP, Zheng Y (2023), Plants 12(3):422, Figure 5.
evidence.claim_scope: Controlled calcium-withholding symptom progression in the tested cultivar/system; not a universal field diagnostic signature.

media.provenance: Punja et al. 2019, Frontiers in Plant Science 10:1120, Figure 4; repository original images/reference/original/frontiers-cannabis-botrytis-figure-4.webp

observations.finding: The source figure combines plant phenotypes, harvested-flower decay, culture and microscopy panels.
observations.pattern: flower decay and associated laboratory morphology

differential.label: Botrytis-associated gray mold / bud rot
discriminating_checks: Use plant-linked lab identification when species-level confirmation matters.
Separate phenotype panels from culture/microscopy evidence.

differential.label: other flower-rot causes including Fusarium/Penicillium-associated decay
discriminating_checks: Inspect fresh tissue and obtain culture/molecular confirmation where appropriate.

uncertainty.reason: Appearance of brown/gray flower decay is not species-specific and the composite contains laboratory evidence unavailable from an ordinary user photo.

evidence.citation: Punja ZK et al. (2019), Frontiers in Plant Science 10:1120, Figure 4.
evidence.claim_scope: Cannabis Botrytis disease reference with phenotype, culture and microscopy context; visual phenotype alone does not prove species.

media.provenance: Thweatt & Kesheimer 2026, Agronomy 16:651, Figure 1; repository original images/reference/original/media-two-spotted-spider-mite-hemp-figure-1.png

observations.finding: The figure presents a standardized 0-5 damage progression from no visible injury through stippling/chlorosis to extensive necrosis and dense webbing.

differential.label: two-spotted spider mite injury
discriminating_checks: Confirm mites or eggs on leaf undersides with magnification.
Do not infer the mite species from stippling alone.

differential.label: other causes of stippling/chlorosis
discriminating_checks: Check for other arthropods and abiotic/nutrient stress when mites are not observed.

uncertainty.reason: Damage signs support a spider-mite differential but visual injury alone is not definitive species confirmation.

evidence.citation: Thweatt IN, Kesheimer K (2026), Agronomy 16:651, Figure 1.
evidence.treatment: Tetranychus urticae herbivory / standardized damage scoring
evidence.claim_scope: Standardized hemp damage progression associated with T. urticae exposure; confirmation should include mites/eggs rather than symptoms alone.
